column1: # tools/live-gate-budget.tsv -- the crossing budget of plan_entity.md §5.
# One row per stage of the live gate, RECORDED FROM A BUILD rather than chosen:
# `tools/live-gate --record` writes this file from the run it just did.
# INBOUND ONLY. These are native->managed thunk entries (Crossings' own
# qualifier); the managed->engine direction belongs to step 0e's probes.
# TWO KINDS OF ROW, AND THE `gated_on` COLUMN SAYS WHICH
# gated_on=rate   the stage ran >= 20 server frames, so it HAS a rate. Enforced
#                 on ceiling_per_frame = recorded_per_frame*1.5 + 10, from ONE
#                 sample. A rate over that many frames is stable, so one sample
#                 is an estimate and this ceiling is TIGHT: hot-reload runs at
#                 97% of its ceiling and is meant to.
# gated_on=total  the stage is too short for a rate (5 frames is nearly all
#                 fixed cost, and one frame either way moves a rate by tens).
#                 Enforced on ceiling_total = total_max*1.5 + 200, where
#                 total_max is the LARGEST of `samples` measurements, not one
#                 of them. This ceiling is DELIBERATELY LOOSE and the columns
#                 say by how much: total_min..total_max is the observed spread.
#                 `die` has been measured between 481 and 1403 with no code
#                 change behind it -- 2.9x. A ceiling built from 1.5x one draw
#                 from that sits below the stage's own median, which is exactly
#                 the bug this schema replaced.
# So: to tell a loose ceiling from a tight one, read `gated_on`, then
# total_min..total_max against ceiling_total. A row whose spread is a factor of
# three is loose because the quantity is, and it says so in its own columns.
# THE §5 RATCHET, AND WHAT IT RATCHETS ON
# §5: "the initial budget is whatever Phase 0 measures on today's build; each
# phase may only lower it." A row may move DOWN freely. Moving one UP is
# governed by evidence, not by prohibition, because the two directions are not
# symmetric:
#   * a rate ceiling never rises. --record rewrites it from one sample and
#     --record-totals does not touch it at all.
#   * a total ceiling rises only when `samples` >= 4. Below that --record
#     KEEPS the ceiling already on disk and prints why, so a lane cannot widen
#     a short stage as a side effect of the run that failed on it. One 2-pass
#     run is 2 samples; a raise takes at least two deliberate runs merged with
#     `tools/live-gate --record-totals`.
# That distinction is the whole point. Relaxing a limit because your change
# cost more is what §5 forbids. Correcting a ceiling that was computed from a
# bad measurement -- one draw from a 2.9x-wide distribution -- is not relaxing
# a limit, because there was never a measurement there to relax. The sample
# count in each row is what lets a reader tell those two apart.
# The ratchet has a FLOOR under it in the other direction, or "down is free"
# would walk a total ceiling straight back into the bug: record on a quiet
# night, draw N low samples, and the ceiling sinks below the stage's own
# population again. tools/live-gate's SHORT_STAGE_FLOOR holds the largest total
# this project has ever measured for a stage, and a ceiling is never recorded
# below it. For `die` that is 1403, from the eighteen busy-box measurements in
# .claude/entity-port/status/diag-saveload.md.
# WHAT A TOTAL-GATED CEILING CAN AND CANNOT CATCH -- SAY IT RATHER THAN IMPLY IT
# `die` costs between 481 and 1403 inbound crossings with no code change behind
# it. Any ceiling that does not fail on that spread cannot detect a regression
# smaller than the spread. That is a property of the measurement, not a choice
# made here, and no formula fixes it:
#   CAN catch    a gross regression -- a per-entity crossing appearing where a
#                per-frame one used to be, an added round trip per ragdoll
#                bone. Those are 3x-and-up and go straight through the ceiling.
#   CANNOT catch a 20% rise. Nothing gated on an 8-frame total can.
# So what else guards these four stages? Honestly: less than guards the other
# thirteen, and that is worth knowing rather than papering over.
#   * the PER_FRAME_OPS invariants (ServerFrame and friends, exactly one per
#     server frame) do NOT apply: they need >= 30 frames, and a 1/8 reset
#     artefact is bigger than their 0.05 tolerance.
#   * the four stages' WORK is nearly all counted somewhere else. `join`'s
#     entity creation shows up in the map load the gate waits on; `die`'s
#     ragdoll and `damage`'s traces recur inside `shoot` and `respawn`, which
#     are rate-gated over hundreds of frames at 270.120 and 221.149. A change
#     that made dying expensive would move those too.
#   * the steps' own PASS/FAIL assertions are unaffected by any of this. A
#     ragdoll that stops spawning fails `die` on behaviour, not on budget.
# And one hole, named rather than hidden: `die` is BIMODAL. It ran 8 server
# frames in 14 of this lane's 16 calibration passes and 28-30 in the other two.
# A long pass is checked against ceiling_per_frame, which for a total-gated row
# came from the SHORT run -- 735/8 = 91.875 -> 147.812 -- while the stage
# actually runs at 710/30 = 23.7 when it is long. So a long `die` is checked
# against a ceiling six times its own rate and cannot fail. The gate PRINTS a
# note when that happens rather than a silent tick. Fixing it properly means
# recording two ceilings for a bimodal stage, and nothing has needed that yet.
# The one thing that would make these tight is more frames per stage, and that
# is a change to what the steps DO, which belongs to whoever owns them.
# AND THE RATE ROWS HAVE THE SAME PROBLEM. MEASURED 2026-09-06.
# Everything above treats a rate as the STABLE normalisation -- "a rate over
# that many frames is stable, so one sample is an estimate and this ceiling is
# TIGHT". The `projectile` row was added on 2026-09-06 and its first two
# recordings falsified that, on an unchanged build, in the same worktree, on
# the same map, an hour apart:
#     run 1  pass 1   48711 crossings / 1378 frames =  35.349 per frame
#     run 1  pass 2   53647 crossings / 1520 frames =  35.294
#     run 2  pass 1  306211 crossings / 1554 frames = 197.047
#     run 2  pass 2  339964 crossings / 1538 frames = 221.043
# 6.3x, over fifteen hundred frames. And it is NOT this stage: the whole run
# moves together. Every rate-gated stage, run 1 against run 2, first pass:
# So a run lands in one of two regimes and a rate row recorded in the quiet one
# fails in the busy one. That is not hypothetical: `projectile` was first
# recorded at 63.024 from run 1 and the very next gate run failed it twice, at
# 197.047 and 221.043, with nothing changed in between. The ceiling here is
# re-derived from run 2 -- the SAME REGIME EVERY OTHER ROW IN THIS FILE WAS
# RECORDED IN, which is the only thing that makes it comparable to its
# neighbours (recorded_per_frame: move 192.918, jump 188.384, shoot 173.413,
# push 202.234, trigger 183.147, projectile 197.047). It is a bad measurement
# corrected, in the header's own sense above, and the failure that forced the
# correction is written here rather than quietly dropped.
# WHAT THIS MEANS FOR EVERY ROW BELOW, said plainly: a stage whose cost varies
# 6x with nothing changed cannot detect a regression smaller than 6x, and that
# is now known to apply to the RATE rows and not only to the four total ones.
# The rows are not wrong -- they were all recorded in the busy regime and they
# do catch a gross regression there -- but a gate run that lands in the quiet
# regime is checking every stage against a ceiling roughly 8x its own cost.
# NOT DIAGNOSED. The cause is a crossing that fires ~165 more times per server
# frame in one regime than the other; the per-op breakdown is in
# `debug-api status`.crossings.ops and no run above captured it. Whoever owns the
# budget should record ops-level evidence before tightening any rate row, and
# a second sample per row would be worth more than a tighter formula.
# WOULD A RATE BE BETTER AFTER ALL? MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED.
# The premise of MIN_FRAMES_FOR_RATE is that a short stage's total is the more
# stable of its two normalisations. Over 78 short passes from this lane's ten
# gate runs that is true for two of the four stages and false for the other two:
#   stage      n   total spread     rate spread    ceiling / typical cost
#   shutdown  20   597..732 1.2x    102..305 3.0x   total 2.0x   rate 1.6x
# `join` and `die` scale with frames (per-frame work); `damage` and `shutdown`
# are fixed cost, so more frames only means more idle ones. But the number that
# decides whether a gate is strict -- ceiling over TYPICAL cost -- lands within
# a fifth of 2x for both normalisations on three of the four, and `join` is loose
# either way because its cost genuinely varies six-fold. Picking a
# normalisation per stage off n=20 would be over-fitting for no measurable
# gain, so the total is kept for all four. Recorded here so the next person
# does not have to re-derive it.
# THE `render` ROW IS PER CLIENT FRAME (plan_client_novalve.md 3.3, C0 item 6). step_render reads
# the local client's own counters (/client/{slot}/status) over >= 300 client frames at the spawn
# pose, so its recorded_per_frame and ceiling_per_frame are client crossings per client frame,
# not per server frame like every other row. Recorded at e1694de2 (debug, one 2-pass gate run,
# lane census, 2026-10-04) through live-gate's own write_budget over that run's two samples
# only, so no other row moved: pass 1 3441/323 = 10.653, pass 2 6372/303 = 21.030. The two
# passes differ 2x in their op mix (pass 1 led by ClientStage 1035, ClientStandaloneDraw 969;
# pass 2 by ClientStage 2121, ClientOnCreateMove 1062, ClientMd5PseudoRandom 1062), so the
# header's regime caveat applies here too; a second run is worth more than a tighter ceiling.
# THE `view-camera` ROW (lane camproto, 2026-10-05) was recorded alone: `tools/live-gate --steps
# join,view-camera --record` into a COPY of this file, and only its view-camera row moved here, so no
# other row moved. Debug, on client-cam-proto at dd212f00: pass 1 8706/858 = 10.147,
# pass 2 8467/821. Per server frame, like every row but `render`; the stage cycles cs_cl_overview
# 1/2/0 for nine seconds, so the second view's own client-side crossings are not in it.
